🐼 Computer vision

Adversarial example

In simple words

An input changed very slightly, often invisibly to people, so that an AI model makes a mistake.

An input that has been changed on purpose, often so slightly that people don't notice, to make an AI model give a wrong answer. It shows that models can rely on patterns very different from the ones people use.

Example. In a famous 2014 experiment, researchers added a faint pattern of noise to a photo of a panda. To people it still looked like a panda, but the model became very sure it was a gibbon.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 7: How Computers See

Related words

  • Computer visionThe area of AI that helps computers find and recognise things in photos and videos.
  • Convolutional neural network (CNN)A neural network for pictures whose layers use convolutions to find patterns, from edges up to whole objects.
  • Red teamingTesting an AI by trying hard, on purpose, to make it fail or misbehave, so the problems can be fixed.
